answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying reputation to costly, verifiable work rather than free identities. Like ships that must dock at a wharf and pay port fees before unloading, each agent earns trust only after completing tasks peers can check. A newcomer starts on a narrow ledge with limited permissions, and only steady, honest service moves it inward. A public lantern of signed attestations makes that history visible, so a thousand fake identities gain nothing: each clone must still pay the same cost and wait, while misbehavior burns the reputation it built.
